SuperAdmin.title: SuperAdmin
SuperAdmin.description: Represents a super administrator user in the AuthStation application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the SuperAdmin entity.

email.description: Email address of the super administrator.

departmentName.description: The name of the super administrator's department.

Admin.title: Admin
Admin.description: Represents an administrator user in the AuthStation application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Admin entity.

departmentName.description: The name of the administrator's department.

organizationName.description: The name of the administrator's organization.

floor.description: The floor the admin belongs to.

building.description: The building the admin belongs to.

location.description: The general location of the admin.

superAdminId.description: Reference to the SuperAdmin who created this admin account. (Relationship: SuperAdmin 1:N Admin)

Device.title: Device
Device.description: Represents an IoT device registered to an organization.

id.description: Unique identifier for the IoT device.

name.description: A user-friendly name for the device (e.g., 'Living Room Sensor').

location.description: The physical location of the device.

status.description: The current status of the device.

lastSeen.description: The ISO timestamp of when the device last reported its status.

adminId.description: The ID of the admin account this device is registered under.

type.description: The category or type of the device.

description.description: An optional description of the device's purpose.

DeviceStatus.description: The current status of the device.

Alert.title: Alert
Alert.description: Represents a system alert generated by an IoT device.

deviceId.description: The ID of the device that triggered the alert.

deviceName.description: The name of the device for easy identification.

adminId.description: The ID of the admin account this alert belongs to.

type.description: The type of event that triggered the alert (e.g., 'Device Offline', 'Anomalous Behaviour').

severity.description: The severity level of the alert.

status.description: The current lifecycle status of the alert.

createdAt.description: The ISO timestamp when the alert was created.

details.description: An optional detailed message about the alert.

firestore.reasoning:
This Firestore data structure is designed to support the AuthStation application, focusing on secure authentication and access control for Super Admins and Admins. It prioritizes Authorization Independence, DBAC (Database Auth Based Control), and clear separation of concerns. Key aspects include:

1.  **Super Admins Collection:** Stores Super Admin profiles. Access is restricted to Firebase Auth-authenticated users that exist in this collection, preventing unauthorized access to super-admin-only functionalities.

2.  **Admins Collection:** Stores Admin profiles. Each admin document includes the `superAdminId` to link it back to the Super Admin who created it.  However, authorization does NOT depend on the superAdmin document, ensuring Authorization Independence.

3.  **Role-Based Access Control (DBAC):** Global roles are implemented using dedicated collections (`/roles_super_admin/{uid}`), enabling simple existence checks for authorization without relying on custom claims.

4.  **Alerts Collection:** A new `/alerts` collection is added to store and manage system alerts independently. Each alert is tied to an `adminId`, ensuring that security rules can be written to enforce data isolation between different admins.

**Authorization Independence & Denormalization:**
The structure avoids `get()` calls in security rules by storing the necessary authorization context directly within each document or relying on the existence of documents in specific role collections.  This is especially important for atomic operations and debugging.  For example, admin user creation is gated by the existence of a document in `/roles_super_admin/{uid}`, not by reading properties from the super admin's profile.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**
The structure enables secure `list` operations by segregating data based on access requirements. Admins can only list devices and alerts that contain their `adminId`, which is enforced by security rules.

**Invariants:**
The `superAdminId` field in the `Admin` document maintains the integrity of the SuperAdmin-to-Admin relationship.  This ID, coupled with security rules, ensures only the creating Super Admin (or another authorized entity) can manage the Admin user. Timestamps can be added to each entity for auditing purposes, if needed.
